import href.description: Type-safe path builder backed by the generated route types.

href().description:
Build a URL from a route pattern with full type-checking of both the pattern and its params.
A typo in the path or a missing param is a compile error, unlike a hand-written string.

import generatePath.description: Interpolate params into a path pattern (untyped counterpart of `href`).

generatePath().description:
Fill a path pattern with params at runtime.
Prefer `href()` in Framework mode — it validates the pattern against the real routes.

import matchPath.description: Match a single pattern against a pathname.

matchPath().description:
Match one pattern against a pathname, returning params or `null`.
For "is this link active" prefer `useMatch()`, which reads the current location itself.

import matchRoutes.description: Match a route array against a location.

matchRoutes().description:
Run the router's matching algorithm manually against a route array.
Useful on the server or in tests to find which routes a URL would render.

import resolvePath.description: Resolve a relative `to` against a pathname.

resolvePath().description:
Resolve a relative path into an absolute `Path` object.
Inside components `useResolvedPath()` does this against the current location.

import createPath / parsePath.description: Convert between a `Path` object and a URL string.

createPath().description: Serialize a `{ pathname, search, hash }` object into a URL string.

parsePath().description: Parse a URL string into `{ pathname, search, hash }`.

import createSearchParams.description: Build a `URLSearchParams` from an object or entry list.

createSearchParams().description: Construct `URLSearchParams`, accepting array values (`{ tag: ['a', 'b'] }`) unlike the native constructor.

import renderMatches.description: Render the element tree for a set of matches.

renderMatches().description: Turn the result of `matchRoutes()` into React elements. Pairs with manual matching on the server.
